name: Aviern
long_description: Aviern makes unmanned cargo airplanes for commercial operations and defense logistics. In 2 months we built our own scaled aircraft that taxis, takes off, flies and lands fully autonomously and are working on a larger 50lb aircraft.

launches.title: Aviern: Unmanned cargo airplanes for autonomous airports
launches.tagline: Fixed-wing drones for regional air freight and defense logistics. 1000lbs carried over 1000 miles under $1000.
launches.body:
We’re building unmanned cargo airplanes to fly freight to every one of America’s 5,000 public-use airports, and to resupply the military where a crewed flight is too costly or too dangerous.

Our scaled composite prototype already takes off, flies a route, and lands on its own. We designed, built, and flew it in under two months.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=125455&key=user_uploads/3391574/b8b7c4b6-95ca-4d38-b5c7-038b5095bb3a)
[ ](https://youtu.be/RPzu5FBxUgg)
I ([Kush Agarwal](https://www.linkedin.com/in/kushhansagarwal/)) spent four years at UCLA building autonomous drones, then got my pilot’s license flying out of small airports across California. All these airports have a short runway with a few Cessnas.

The US has about 5,000 public-use airports like this, and almost every American lives within 30 miles of one. Almost all of them see nothing but general aviation, and they make a great spot for autonomous cargo airplanes.

[Arvin Singh](https://linkedin.com/in/arvin-singh-b0b1a7240?utm_source=share_via&utm_content=profile&utm_medium=member_ios) has designed and built airplanes for 10 years and has won international aircraft design and flight competitions, where you win by carrying the most payload on the lightest airframe. 

Airplanes transport $8.3 trillion of goods a year, a third of world trade by value, but in the US that network stops at a few hundred airports. Only about 520 are certified for airline service. Past that, everything moves by truck.

The military has a similar problem. In Afghanistan, one soldier or contractor was killed or wounded for every 24 fuel convoys. Contested logistics, disaster relief, and remote resupply all need cargo flown where a crewed flight is too expensive, too risky, or impossible to staff.

We are making it possible for packages to move autonomously, and it starts by building an aircraft fit for the job.

**Solution**

We’re designing cargo aircraft from scratch with no one on board. With no cockpit, seats, or life support, the whole fuselage carries cargo.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=125455&key=user_uploads/3391574/72b04b12-3bc3-47a8-accf-68ead30e2c88)

Our first aircraft will be a purpose-built airframe under 1,320 lb, designed from day one for proposed Part 108 rules. That gives us a path to commercial cargo flights in years, not a decade.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=125455&key=user_uploads/3391574/f5b1a505-a74e-48db-9dfa-fb984e68e66f)

We start on the routes regional carriers fly today: feeder flights from integrator hubs to small airports. The same platform serves defense resupply, delivering urgent cargo into constrained environments without putting a crew at risk.

**What we have built**

We have a self-flying aircraft and a full autonomy stack. Our aircraft take off, fly a route, and land with no pilot in the loop. We built the airframe, autopilot, perception, and ground software in-house.

**What’s next**

* **By Q1 2027:** Fly a retrofitted small airplane fully autonomously, with no one on board controlling it. This proves our autonomy stack on a real certified airframe.
* **By Q1 2028:** Build and fly our clean-sheet cargo aircraft, followed by commercial operations.

The same autonomy stack scales up to larger cargo aircraft and defense missions.

The end state is fully autonomous airports, where aircraft load, launch, fly, land, and turn around with no humans in the operation. Connected together, those airports form a network that moves freight around the clock. We believe autonomous aircraft will become the backbone of how the country moves goods.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=125455&key=user_uploads/3391574/8080f195-f492-4318-bf54-6a4021b9ca2c)

**Our asks**

Introductions to

* **Feeder program leads** at FedEx, UPS, and DHL and other carriers
* **Shippers moving urgent, high-value goods by air** such as medical supplies, aircraft parts, semiconductors
* **Defense logistics** stakeholders such as military bases, units, or elsewhere in the Department of War working on logistics
